headline: Every battery, at your fingertips
lede: Missile Command got its arcade control law back: keys 1, 2 and 3 fire the left, center and right batteries from anywhere on the board — and the phone gets a FAST button for the expert's shot.

notes.text: The original wired one button to each battery; aim chose the target, never the launcher. Keys 1/2/3 now work exactly that way — key 2 calls the fast center battery from any sector, the arcade's own answer to a smart bomb at distance.
Phone players get a labeled FAST pad button; the board teaches the whole law itself — every battery wears its key number, and the center glows cyan while smart bombs are live.

The kick target this week — the arcade's games 18-34 dial table — is documented as BLOCKED: the per-number values exist only in the original's service chart, outside our sources, and fidelity means not inventing them. The audit trail is on #3695.
Proof: 126 sim checks, 35 mutants all dead, 13 checks in real Chrome. Mouse players lose nothing — the nearest-battery click law and Space still replay byte-identical.

look.text: Call the fast battery from any corner — keys 1/2/3, or the FAST button
